## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The change breaks default loading, rejects a valid port, and hides configuration errors. Host normalization also has a documentation mismatch and an uncovered branch.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file makes `load_defaults()` in `app/startup.py:6` raise `FileNotFoundError` on every call. Restore the file or update the loader to obtain its defaults elsewhere. — Callers can no longer load the bundled default configuration.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False`, although the documented range includes 65535. Change the upper comparison to `<= 65535`. — A valid TCP port is rejected.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — A missing configuration file or malformed JSON is swallowed by `except Exception` and returned as `{}` without any diagnostic. Propagate the error or provide a caller-visible failure signal. — Callers cannot distinguish a failed configuration load from a valid empty configuration.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says “returns None when h is empty,” but the empty-input branch executes `return ""`. Update the docstring to describe the actual result. — Callers following the documentation may check for `None` and miss empty hosts.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — The trailing-dot branch has no test; the existing normalization test exercises only case conversion. Add an assertion such as `normalize_host("Example.COM.") == "example.com"`. — Regressions that leave the trailing dot intact would pass the current tests.

## Strengths
- The added millisecond timeout test checks that `"1500ms"` converts to `1.5` seconds.
- The configuration success test reads a real temporary JSON file and checks the parsed result.
